precepts.text: These are they that were not defiled with women. If our weakness is the woman, the 144, their weakness will not be woman.
precepts.point: A woman weakness is what? If our weakness is the woman, okay, that's why God says in Revelation 14, the 144, their weakness will not be woman. He says these are they that were not defiled with who?

note.label: The Decayed State of Liberal Women

precepts.why:
For the last sixty years a war has been waged on the black community, and Esau has been exploiting our weakness. What is the black man's weakness? The black woman. Peter calls her “the weaker vessel”: she is weaker than us. When Satan waged war against Adam, did he come and trick Adam? No. He went through Adam's weakness, the woman, to take Adam down. And the white man understands that too.

That is why God says of the 144 in Revelation 14, “These are they which were not defiled with women”. If our weakness is the woman, the 144's weakness will not be woman. They overcome the very place where Satan took Adam down.

And the woman's weakness is her emotions. She can be manipulated; the white man can trick her. Satan played with Eve's emotions, and she said the serpent beguiled me. Sisters, learn to control your emotions. In the house the sisters get in their feelings; that is their weakness, and our weakness is them.

We come down hard on the sisters because of the important role a woman plays in the nation. Y'all don't understand your importance, but our enemy does. He says, to destroy the black man I have to destroy the black woman first: make her a liberal, destroy the household, take the man out of it, make her think she doesn't need a man. The white man tricked you, sisters. So many problems in the black community come from no father in the house.

A strong woman and an independent woman are two different things. Our righteous foremothers were strong women: a strong woman builds her husband, keeps the family together, and uses her good job to help her family. An independent woman, the liberal woman, oppresses her husband, argues with him, won't listen to him, and ultimately leaves him seeking happiness. Your grandmother before the sixties was good, but the women from the 1960s until now, the majority of their minds are destroyed. The man who dwells with his wife according to knowledge must know where the weakness lies.

precepts.point: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison. We are the spirits in prison that he preached to. You have Christians talking about, did he go under the ground? No. We are in a prison house. Being dominated by another race is a prison. Christ came to us while Rome dominated us and he preached to us.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Christ “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. We are the spirits in prison that he preached to. Christians ask, did he go under the ground? No. Being dominated by another race is a prison, and Christ came to us while Rome dominated us and preached to us.

Wisdom shows what kind of prison it is. This is about ancient Egypt, but watch what it says about the Egyptians and how it relates to us: “So then whosoever there fell down was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars”. Just like the ancient Egyptians in that sea of darkness were shut up in a prison without iron bars, that is what we are in today. There are no iron bars, so people say, I'm free, there are no shackles on me. It is the same thing.

Isaiah said we are “hid in prison houses”, and those prison houses are democracy, Republicans, socialism, liberals, Baptists, Episcopal. So the message for our people is Isaiah 49:9: “That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves.” Come out of that cage.

And Zechariah shows the way out: “by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” The blood of the covenant is Christ dying on the cross. The prisoners are you and me; the pit is Babylon, where there is no water, no truth being taught besides what we are teaching. “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: the stronghold is the commandments in the name of Christ. The Christ who preached to the spirits in prison is the one who brings us out of this prison without bars.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel.” Failure to dwell with his wife according to knowledge is another of the things husbands do that destroy marriages, and ruling your own house well depends on it.

A wise husband studies his wife: her fears, her emotions, her struggles, her strengths. That is dwelling with her according to knowledge. When you understand your wife, you are able to guide your house. You push her toward greatness, but you also know her limits, and because you know them you set things up in the home so that things can work. If your wife is emotionally not there to deal with certain things, then you set it up another way. In order to lead, you have to know what they deal with, what they are able to do and what they are not able to do. That goes for your kids as well. You do it now without realizing it: you understand strengths and weaknesses, and you prioritize based on that.

Some men never learn their wives and then wonder why the marriage feels distant.

The other things that destroy a house show the same failure to know her: bitterness and harshness, holding things over her after she has repented and humiliating her, when you are supposed to love your wife as your own self; neglect, when a trip to Walmart is an exciting event for her because you haven’t taken her out, while ordering the house and dealing with the kids all the time is difficult; and withholding love and affection, because if she is not getting it from you, where is she going to get it from? A bishop rules his own house well by dwelling with his wife according to knowledge and giving her honour.

precepts.text: The angels that sinned here are the sons of God in Genesis 6, Seth's line that messed around with the daughters of men. And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness. What was Noah? A preacher of righteousness. When it says God was longsuffering, what was he doing? Noah was preaching repentance: y'all better repent, the Most High going to destroy this place. They said: you crazy. Look at that dummy building a boat for no reason. Noah was prophesying all that time because God was longsuffering. He gave them a hundred years. They did not listen.
precepts.point: When once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah: the Lord gave a hundred year time span for the people to repent.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment”. The angels that sinned are the sons of God in Genesis 6: Seth's line, that messed around with the daughters of men.

“And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”. What was Noah? A preacher of righteousness. So when 1 Peter says “the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing”, what was God doing? He was giving them time, and Noah was preaching repentance the whole while: y'all better repent, the Most High going to destroy this place. They said, you crazy. Look at that dummy building a boat for no reason.

Noah was prophesying all that time because God was longsuffering. He gave them a hundred years to repent, and they did not listen, and only “eight souls were saved by water”.

That is why Peter joins it to Christ, who was “put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”: a man, not a demigod, brought back to life by the spirit after three days, who “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. Those spirits in prison are his people, us in captivity. As Noah preached righteousness to a world that would not hear, Christ preached to his people in prison, and the longsuffering of God is waiting on us to repent the same way it waited in the days of Noah.

precepts.text: The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us: not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, which is the water we read about in Isaiah 1:16, but the answer of a good conscience toward God by the resurrection of Jesus Christ. A good conscience toward God means keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ. If you are living in sin when the Lord comes, you will not have a good conscience, and it comes out in your countenance.
precepts.point: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God. Baptism was always symbolic: you are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Water baptism keeps coming up over and over, and this is the verse they use: “The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us.” They say, got you, baptism does save you. But watch the breakdown.

“Not the putting away of the filth of the flesh.” That is the water, the washing we read of in Isaiah 1:16. Peter makes it clear that the water does not save you. What saves is “the answer of a good conscience toward God”, and that comes “by the resurrection of Jesus Christ”.

A good conscience toward God is keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ. If you are a thief, a liar or a child molester when the Lord comes, you will not have a good conscience, and it comes out in your facial expressions. You will not make eye contact; your head is down, because you know there is something troubling you within. That is why Colossians says we are buried with him and “risen with him through the faith of the operation of God”: it is the faith and the changed life, not the water.

precepts.text: Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them. Offenses and fear of tribulation will not make you turn your back on Christ.
precepts.point: Peter laid the instructions for marriages in hard times. We see marriage counsels where a sister is upset because her husband's socks are on the floor, or a sister wants to give up the faith and go back to the world, or a brother wants to be a whoremonger instead of a man of his nation leading his people. There are more trying times coming where you will be worried about surviving; how much more in a household where husband and wife are striving against each other? Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying, and increasing our faith, following the instructions laid forth.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
Peter says, “But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye.” We must begin to learn how to suffer for righteousness' sake, for the sake of Christ. And we are happy in it: that happiness is our peace. Happy are they that keep God's laws.

David shows where that peace comes from: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” Nothing shall offend them means offenses, and being afraid of tribulation, will not make you turn your back on Christ.

That is why Peter goes on, “and be not afraid of their terror”: the terror of being persecuted. Times are not going to get easy, for husband, wife, brother or sister, so we have to prepare ourselves for hard and trying times and not go railing for railing with one another. Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying and increasing our faith, and following the instructions laid forth.

The man or woman who loves God's law has a peace the world cannot shake. When the tribulation comes, the law they love keeps them from being offended, and they endure it happy, suffering for righteousness' sake.

precepts.text: Hast thou a wife after thy mind? Forsake her not. A woman after your mind understands that she is in subjection to you, that what you want is what she wants; she makes your desires her desires, your aspirations her aspirations, because her desire is unto her husband, not unto herself. Her job as the manager of the house is to make sure the head of it is happy. But the world told her, no, it is yours, sis; do what you want to do.
precepts.point: Video played in class: they turned you against black men by selling you fear disguised as standards, highlighting his mistakes but hiding the obstacles, making struggle look like incompetence, rewarding you every time you blamed him instead of the system, turning your pain into content, and convincing you he is the only man who must be perfect to be worthy.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“Hast thou a wife after thy mind? forsake her not”. Very few understand that this is not their show. It is about the house of her husband. A wife after your mind is a woman who understands that she is in subjection to you and that you are the head of the home, so what you want is what she wants. She makes your desires her desires. Your aspirations become her aspirations. How you want things to be becomes how she wants things to be, because she understands her desire is unto her husband, not unto herself.

If her husband wants the environment this way, she makes the environment that way. If he wants the household this way, she makes the household this way. That is her job as the manager of the house: to make sure the CEO is happy. That is what a woman is supposed to do. But the world told her, no, it's yours, sis, you do what you want to do.

That is the last of the ten signs that she does not respect the Christ in you: she does not follow your lead spiritually, does not align with your direction in this truth, and picks and chooses what to follow. A wife after your mind is the opposite, and that is the wife Peter speaks of. By being in subjection to her own husband, her chaste conversation can win even a man that obeys not the word. The one who used to be loud and argue now does what he asks without challenging his authority, and he says, the word did that? Let me go see what those brothers in purple and gold are talking about.

Through submission you can move mountains with a man. When she knows she is right and still stands down because he is the head and has the final say, he is left with hot coals on his head, knowing she is more righteous than he is. It changes a man. That is a wife not to forsake.

precepts.text: Wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, that if any obey not the word they may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives, while they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. A sister at a Passover panel asked when she could leave a husband of ten years who had followed her through Africanism and Islam; to him this truth is one more fad until he sees it is real. Come home disciplined, not cursing him out, dressed properly, and tell him you want him to take command. If he is righteous he comes in behind you; the same goes for a brother who repented last week and wants to turn the house upside down this week. Many wives have said, I did not know he was this serious, he was willing to let me go, and came in. The timetable is the Lord's, not your hormones.
precepts.point: Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her, because she was his portion and was meant to destroy him. Some are not made to make it; if your spirit is not girded, one of these temptations takes you.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Before anyone walks away, look at the other side. At a Passover panel years ago a sister asked when she could walk away from her husband in the world. They had been together about ten years, through Africanism, through Islam, through different things. In his mind this truth might be just another fad. Wait, sister. Lean back.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” He is worldly, but he isn't telling you to break the laws of God, so still deal with him properly. Chaste means with discipline: you aren't cursing him out. He watches the change in you, sees the fear of the Lord in you, and sees it is serious, not a phase.

“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, “the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.” She puts on proper clothing, and tells him: my husband, I want you to come in and take command, so I can deal with you as a proper wife. He comes home from catching hell at work and she knows how to pull him out of it, and he asks, where are you learning this wisdom? If he is righteous, he comes in behind you; we have seen it many times.

Men do the same: a brother who was in sin with his wife last week wants to turn the house upside down this week. Give her a chance to see you're serious. Wives have said, I didn't know he was this serious; he was willing to let me go, and they came in behind him. That is the Most High giving righteousness to righteousness.

precepts.point: 1 Timothy 5:8: if any provide not for his own house, he hath denied the faith and is worse than an infidel. Hard times may have the wife hold it down for a while, as in Tobit, but Tobit did not quit and figure out what he wanted to be when he grew up. Brothers here have destabilized whole households playing around with a business because the wife makes good money, taking more risk with more lives on the line than they ever took alone.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”. The knowledge and the honour you give is the commitment to play your role as a husband in all matters. Not, this is the wife you gave me. Not complaining, and not hating her, because the scripture says no man ever hated his own flesh. You deal with the situation.

Men have a moral sense in us, most of us, though some are full of error and lack that integrity. “The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him”. Integrity is doing what's right when nobody's looking, when nobody is there to hold you accountable, like Paul said, not in my presence only. A just man moves with integrity in how he manages and steers his household and in everything else he does as a man of God.

And his children are blessed after him because he raised a stable, sound household. Dwelling with your wife according to knowledge and giving her honour is part of that provision, leadership, instruction and honour the husband owes the house, the same duty Exodus 21:10 says he shall not diminish.

precepts.text: Every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour.
precepts.point: Every man should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour, and wash his wife with the water of the word.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
Peter tells the husbands to “dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”. Nobody understands what that honour means. The women think it means give me mercy, I'm a woman, I'm the weaker vessel, let me mess up. And some of the men think that too. Paul shows one portion of what it really is: “That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour”.

First, that is talking about you. This body is your vessel, and you need to know how to possess it. But when you get a wife, you take her into your possession, and now you possess her vessel too, because woman came from man. So “his vessel” is your body and her body, and both are to be kept in sanctification, cleansing, and in honour.

The sisters need to examine themselves in reverence and get in line. But brothers, we are the ones with the preeminence to make that happen. A man cannot sit back and wait her out, hoping she leaves so the unbelieving can depart; that is evil as hell too. Dwelling with her according to knowledge means taking hold of your own vessel and hers and making the house right.

precepts.text: That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.
precepts.point: Every man should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour, and wash his wife with the water of the word.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
This is where the man presents his wife to himself, the way Christ does the church: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing”. The honour given to the weaker vessel is the husband washing her with the word, cleansing and sanctifying her until she is without spot.

So you can't do like Adam and say it's the woman you gave me. You had choices. There were proving processes that should have been done properly and correctly, with the right time constraints, before she became yours. And once she is yours, there is no divorce in that. You are in it.

We can either be happy and function the way the Lord says we should function, or the man will give you the version of himself that he needs to survive. David never touched Michal again; he did not divorce her, but that was it, it dried up. A man can tolerate that much longer than a woman can. We should not be bitter and we should not hold one another in contempt. We have to build that thing up.

precepts.text: If there be kindness, meekness and comfort in her tongue, her husband is not like other men.
precepts.point: Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel.” It is not saying a woman can’t have the outward adorning. Some think a woman has to look bummy and can’t get dressed up. Sisters can plait their heads and get fixed up; just don’t let your glory be in that, because a woman can be all hooked up and her spirit rotten. “But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, meaning Christ is in her spirit, “even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.”

What that hidden adorning sounds like, Sirach tells: “If there be kindness, meekness, and comfort, in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.” A man who has a woman like this is not like most men, who don’t have it. That shows how rare this spirit is. Some brothers hear that verse and melt, because they don’t have it: do women like this even exist? Ask a sister and she can name twenty things she doesn’t like about her husband, but has to rack her brain for one or two good things.

Meek means obedience. Not always screaming, arguing and fighting, when the man just got through dealing with all that in the street and is the one making sure you have a house over your head and heat; you are biting the hand that feeds you. “For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord.” She adorned herself with subjection to her husband, and that is of great price, far above rubies. Not my lord on the phone with the sisters and cursing him as soon as the phone hangs up.

Beauty is corruptible, the clothes are corruptible; those things fade. A righteous spirit stays with you, and that is how you grow old in righteousness together watching the grandkids. Your inner spirit makes your outside look good. When you find a woman with kindness, meekness and comfort in her tongue, you will have paradise in your marriage and not a prison marriage, because husband and wife is the beginning, the nucleus of everything.

precepts.text: The longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah while the ark was preparing, and eight souls were saved by water.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
While the ark was preparing, Noah was not silent. He was a preacher of righteousness telling his people to repent, and “the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing”. The Most High waited for them to repent, and they were disobedient.

In the end “few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.” Understand that: the ones that were actually in the water died. The eight were saved in the ark while the water destroyed everyone else, so this is not talking about getting baptized.

precepts.text: Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, that if any obey not the word, they may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives, beholding your chaste conversation coupled with fear; this is what Abigail was putting in place.
precepts.point: She did not turn her lord over to be destroyed, as some women today would be ready to do; instead she pleaded, Let not my lord regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. She had not seen the young men David sent, or she would have stepped in then to protect their house.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” This is what Abigail was putting in place.

Her chaste conversation was her behavior. When she heard David was coming, she made that feast and brought it down to meet him, to spare her house: “she hasted, and lighted off the ass, and fell before David on her face.”

That is the lesson for wives. If your lord is out of the spirit, instead of going railing for railing with him, your behavior should be able to win him over, to make him say, I am tripping, I have a good wife keeping the commandments who stays in a humble spirit. Provoking with the mouth just leaves an unhappy household, where people living under the same roof are set against each other.

precepts.text: The eyes of the Most High are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers.
precepts.point: The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
David asks, “Give ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.” The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. “For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.” His eyes are over the righteous and his ears are open to their prayers, but his face is against them that do evil.

You have to put yourself in the Bible and see yourself in these scriptures, the way Elder Kena, Bishop and the leadership men teach. David mourns because of the voice of the enemy and the oppression of the wicked who cast iniquity upon him; if we want to be heard the way he was, we have to be among the righteous.

precepts.text: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing.
precepts.point: An eye for an eye is answered with resist not evil. This is not a command to stand and be beaten; it is a command not to pay back evil as though it were owed.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
“An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth” is answered with “ye resist not evil”. Peter says the same: “Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.”

This is not a command to stand and be beaten. It is a command not to pay back evil as though it were owed, not rendering evil for evil or railing for railing. Instead of paying it back, bless, because we are called to inherit a blessing. Turning the other cheek is refusing to collect the debt of evil.

precepts.text: Being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit.
precepts.point: As the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will. To quicken is to make alive, and it covers both the raising of the dead and the making alive of men dead in their sins.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will.” To quicken is to make alive. Peter uses the word of Christ himself: “For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”.

Put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: made alive. The Father raised up the Son; and the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do, and so the Son quickeneth whom he will. Quickening covers both the raising of the dead and the making alive of men dead in their sins.

precepts.text: Baptism doth also now save us, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience; Christ's baptism is based on the conscience, not on washing the body.
precepts.point: Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ”. The baptism that saves is not the putting away of the filth of the flesh; it is the answer of a good conscience toward God.

Christ's baptism is based on the conscience, not on washing the body. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin. What they received by the laying on of the apostles' hands was the cleansing of the conscience through Christ's word.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: Water was used symbolically, and John’s baptism was based on scriptures like this: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings.” That is what it symbolized.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: “For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God”: all that washing makes no change on your inside.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: “And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins”: in the time of John the Baptist they were sincere and confessed their sins. Find anybody on Facebook or YouTube getting dipped in water confessing their sins; all you see is the dip. That is still not following the scriptures.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: A young man once cursed out his parents to go to Passover and was put to death in a car accident on the way back; the last thing his parents heard from him was curses. “Honour thy father with thy whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of thy mother. Remember that thou wast begotten of them; and how canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee?” There is no way you can pay your parents back; all you can do is give glory to the Lord for them.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 1

precepts.why: This is how all of us must be; we cannot have guile, deceit, trickery or craftiness in our mouth. “Let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile”: these are things we must put in practice. It’s not enough just reading it; when you are tempted to speak evil, close your lips. “But the face of the Lord is against them that do evil”: all you men and women who ran out of here and are speaking evil now, the Lord is against you. That’s not something I wrote; I’m reading the scriptures.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: You might think joint-heirs leaves out the woman, but it doesn’t. “Dwell with them according to knowledge”: according to the knowledge of God, the law. “Giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”: yeah, we know she got half a clue, but bear with her. “And as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered”.
